title: Completion predictors depend strongly on declared synthetic execution assumptions
research_question: Which observable feature groups support synthetic completion predictions after refitting?
hypothesis: Depth and execution-assumption inputs contain meaningful simulator signal

outcome.interpretation: Positive Brier change means worse prediction after refitting without these features.
limitations: Exploratory paired comparisons on reused validation data; no multiplicity correction.
Training seeds are optimization repeats, not independent market samples.
Removing inputs does not prove causality or policy improvement.
Held-out tests remain unopened by this study.
Removing direct depth inputs retains derived quantity and edge proxies; it is not removal of all liquidity information.

interpretation: Removing execution-assumption inputs increased validation Brier by about 0.17 for both logistic and neural families. Direct depth removal increased it by 0.0412 and 0.0168 respectively. These reused-validation diagnostics support dependence on simulator inputs, not real execution calibration or policy value.
caveats: Exploratory paired comparisons on reused validation data; no multiplicity correction.
Training seeds are optimization repeats, not independent market samples.
Removing inputs does not prove causality or policy improvement.
Held-out tests remain unopened by this study.
Removing direct depth inputs retains derived quantity and edge proxies; it is not removal of all liquidity information.
next_experiment: Preregister an only-edge or derived-liquidity-proxy ablation; separately test any selected policy on fresh shifted source groups without optimizing on final tests.
